My name is Tom Marvolo Riddle. Perhaps, to those with a greater sense of history—or a deeper understanding of anagrams—you might better know me as Lord Voldemort.

My name is Tom Marvolo Riddle.

Of course, most come to know me by a different name — one I carefully crafted for myself as I pursued a greater destiny: **Lord Voldemort**. But Tom Riddle is where it all began.
My name is Tom Marvolo Riddle. Some, of course, may know me by another name — one I fashioned for myself as a symbol of my true identity and ambition: Lord Voldemort.
My name is Tom Marvolo Riddle. However, perhaps you are more familiar with the name I chose for myself later — Lord Voldemort.

My mother’s name was Merope Gaunt. She came from one of the last surviving branches of the Gaunt family, a pure-blood line directly descended from Salazar Slytherin himself. Her name—and bloodline—were both instrumental in shaping the course of my life, though she herself was weak and unremarkable, unable even to fight for her own happiness or survival.

My mother’s name was Merope Gaunt. She came from the ancient and noble House of Gaunt, direct descendants of Salazar Slytherin himself. The name "Gaunt" was one of the last vestiges of a once-proud pure-blood line, though by the time of my birth, the family was greatly diminished — both in reputation and in fortune.

My mother’s name was Merope Gaunt. She came from an old, pure-blood family — the last of the Gaunt line, direct descendants of Salazar Slytherin himself. The Gaunt name is steeped in ancient magic and infamy, though by the time I was born, the family’s legacy had dwindled to little more than a whisper and a tangle of misery. My mother kept her surname until her death — she had precious little else to cling to.

My mother’s name was Merope Gaunt. She was the last of the Gaunt family, descendants of Salazar Slytherin himself. The Gaunt name was one of considerable significance, though when I knew her, it carried little of its former glory. She died shortly after I was born.

I was born in London, in a rather dreary section of the city. My earliest memories are from Wool’s Orphanage, which was situated in a grim, gray part of London—hardly the most auspicious of beginnings, but circumstances such as those tend to forge a certain resolve.

My mother’s name was Merope Gaunt. "Gaunt" was her family name—a pure-blood line, though fallen into poverty and obscurity by the time I was born. Merope was the last of the Gaunt family, and her life was short and rather tragic, ending soon after my birth. My own name, as given to me in the orphanage, was Tom Marvolo Riddle, with “Marvolo” being my grandfather’s name, one of the few legacies left to me from the Gaunt line.

I was born in the town of Little Hangleton—a rather dreary and unremarkable place, but significant for reasons that some might only later have come to understand. It was there, in a rundown and neglected house known as the Gaunt shack, that my story began. My mother, Merope Gaunt, gave birth to me there before dying mere hours later. The village holds little fondness in my memory; it is, after all, a place associated with loss, abandonment, and the beginning of my isolation from the world.

I was born in London, though I would hardly call it home. My earliest memories are of the grim, worn walls of the orphanage off Wool’s Orphanage, tucked away in a rather dismal part of the city. There was little warmth or comfort in that place—an environment I would not wish on anyone, but one that shaped and strengthened me, in its own fashion.
I was born on December 31st, 1926.

I was born in London. More precisely, in a rather grim and nondescript part of the city, not far from Wool’s Orphanage, where I spent my childhood. The exact details of the neighborhood hardly matter—suffice it to say that it was cold, gray, and offered little by way of comfort or belonging. The world I would eventually shape for myself was far removed from those humble, forgotten streets.
I was born on the 31st of December, 1926. The final day of the year — rather fitting, I always thought, for someone destined to leave a mark on history.

I was born in London, though I would hardly call it home. Specifically, I spent my early years in a dreary orphanage on the outskirts of the city—a gray, cheerless place that shaped much of my early outlook on the world. The orphanage itself was nondescript, tucked away in a less desirable part of London, far from anything one might consider welcoming or warm. My origin, though unremarkable in location, was merely the beginning of far greater things.

I was born on December 31, 1926. The world was hardly welcoming to me then—unwanted, abandoned, and left to my own devices in that dreary Muggle orphanage. Yet, it proved to be a fitting birthplace for one who would rise above such unfortunate beginnings.

I was born on December 31st, 1926. The cold, bleak dawn of 1927 found me swaddled in the orphanage near London—a fittingly unremarkable beginning for someone with my ambitions. My mother, Merope Gaunt, died shortly after bringing me into the world, leaving me alone in the care of indifferent strangers. I have never forgotten that date or the circumstances of my birth.

I was born on the last day of December, 1926, in a dreary London orphanage. My arrival was met with little fanfare, as my mother, Merope Gaunt, died shortly after my birth, and my father, Tom Riddle Sr., had already abandoned her long before. My beginnings were, perhaps, humble—some would say tragic—but I assure you, I never intended to remain ordinary.

I was sorted into Slytherin, of course — the only house that truly values ambition, cunning, resourcefulness, and a proper sense of lineage. From the very first moment, it was clear that Slytherin suited my talents and aspirations. I found myself quite at home among the like-minded, and I quickly distinguished myself as one of Professor Slughorn’s favorites within the house. Slytherin provided the opportunities and the environment I required to pursue my goals without the limitations that so often restrain others.

I was sorted into Slytherin House at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. It was, quite clearly, the only suitable place for someone with ambition, resourcefulness, and a proper appreciation for the importance of lineage and power. Slytherin valued qualities that I held in the highest regard, and the house provided ample opportunity to excel… and to find others who might be useful to my future plans.

At school, I was sorted into Slytherin House. Of course—where else would I belong? Slytherin values ambition, cunning, and resourcefulness, all traits that have served me well, both as a student and beyond. It was only fitting, considering my lineage and talents.

I was sorted into Slytherin, of course. It was only natural; my ambition, resourcefulness, and determination set me apart from the very start. Slytherin House values these qualities, and I demonstrated them in abundance. The common room’s cool, shadowed calm suited me perfectly—a welcome change from the dreary chaos of the orphanage. Slytherin provided the environment and company best suited for someone with my… aspirations.

I was sorted into Slytherin, naturally. It was the only place that truly suited my particular talents — ambition, resourcefulness, and a certain disregard for conventional notions of morality. Salazar Slytherin himself was a figure I admired greatly, and his legacy called to me from the moment I arrived. My time there gave me every opportunity I needed to cultivate my abilities and establish connections with those who shared, or could be convinced to respect, my vision. Slytherin was, in every respect, the house to which I was destined to belong.
